Published online:
September 11, 2026

Geographic focus:
Global (USA, Middle East/Iran war context, Russia/Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Venezuela)

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES]
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES]

Synopsis:
Chevron CEO Mike Wirth warns that crude oil price buffers — previously drawn from stockpiles and sanctions waivers on floating storage — have been exhausted. With the Iran war ongoing and Ukrainian strikes on Russian refinery infrastructure squeezing supply, he sees upside price risks over the coming months. US diesel has hit $6/gallon for the first time, and Brent is up ~8% on the week. Separately, Chevron plans to self-fund a $7bn Venezuelan expansion entirely from in-country cash flows, targeting ~600,000 bpd by 2031.
